title: A Clocked Round
statement: Let $S$ be a deterministic Boolean Turing machine, $A$ a nondeterministic Boolean Turing machine, $x$ a Boolean input, and $m$ a natural number. Suppose a host configuration is clock-ready, meaning it represents a ready configuration of $A$ with yard-head position zero, and suppose $|x|\le m$. For every Boolean choice word $w$ of length $4(m+1)$, if the run of $A$ on $x$ from its initial configuration under the first $m$ bits of $w$ halts with output consisting of the single bit $v$, then the host run halts with output $v$; moreover, if that run of $A$ does not halt with a single-bit output, then the host run is clock-ready.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is a deterministic Boolean Turing machine
$A$ is a nondeterministic Boolean Turing machine
the initial host configuration is clock-ready
